name: St. Lucia
headline: St. Lucia: −0.6% growth in 2025, 0.7% inflation, debt 77% of GDP
sections: St. Lucia is a $2.7 billion economy (2025), the world's 189th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −0.6% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $29K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 3.6% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 0.7% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 9.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 9.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 20.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 77% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 94% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.9% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −5.2% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Net FDI inflows were 7.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 78% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 72.8 years (2024). Population: 182 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
